overall: I could read only one word with confidence: محمد in L05. Several glyphs carry three dots (ڠ / چ / ڽ type) and a ڤ with one dot, and the short groups کو and مو recur. That points to a Southeast-Asian Jawi or Pegon orthography, not to Arabic, Persian or Kurdish. Most of the groups (هج، لکفتو، ڤنتڠ، لڤبیا، مموتد) do not resolve into any Malay, Arabic or Persian words I recognise. So this looks like a short devotional or amuletic text containing a few Arabic religious words (Muhammad, barakat, possibly 'ala kull), or a garbled copy or cipher of one. It is not continuous readable prose.
language_guess: Malay written in Jawi (possibly a Philippine or Indonesian Jawi variety such as Tausug or Maranao, or Javanese Pegon), with Arabic religious loanwords
